Appearance:
 Mr. Devraj Vishwakarma - Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. Ravendra Shukla- G.A. for the State.
 Mr. Sanjeev Singh - Advocate for the objector.

Order 
This second application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C (482 of BNSS) has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. Applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.455/2024 of Police Station-Garh, District-Rewa, (MP) for commission of the offences punishable under Sections 420,
409/34 of IPC.
3. As per the prosecution story, applicant induced complainant to invest money, after stating that he will get the money doubled invested by him and received a sum of Rs.15 Lacs from the complainant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant, after referring to document Annexure A/4, submits that complainant was working as part of syndicate in the liquor shop.
The complainant, Manish and Shashidhar were actually running the liquor ship and present applicant was supervising the same from Bhopal.
With respect to above, learned counsel for the applicant has filed affidavit of various persons as well as photographs to substantiate the aforesaid submissions.
It is also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12478 2 MCRC-10562-2025 urged that applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.

On above grounds, it has been prayed that the applicant be granted the Satish Shukla vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158171796/
1 benefit of anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Satish Shukla vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the application.

6. Learned counsel for the objector/complainant submits that it is evident from the evidence collected by the prosecution that a sum of Rs.15 Las has been credited into the account of applicant and he received the above amount for getting the same doubled.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the application be dismissed.
7. I have learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
8. Perusal of record reveals that earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn on 14.02.2025 and present application has been prepared on 20.02.2025 and filed on 04.03.2025.
In this Court's opinion, there is no change in circumstance after dismissal of the earlier application and documents were already in possession of the applicant.

After perusal of FIR and documents available on the case diary, prima facie , it cannot be said that applicant has been falsely implicated, therefore, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
9. Accordingly, this second application for grant of anticipatory bail is dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Hashmi Satish Shukla vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158171796/
